classification.difficultyReason: Calculate population statistics from data, then use them to standardise a score and estimate a missing raw score.

inlines.text: An assessment task is marked out of 100. The results of the test are shown below.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the mean and population standard deviation for these scores. Answer correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
There are $16$ scores, with $\sum x=1217$ and $\sum x^2=93491$.

$$\begin{align*}\mu&=\frac{1217}{16}\\\mu&=76.0625\\\sigma&=\sqrt{\frac{93491}{16}-\left(\frac{1217}{16}\right)^2}\\\sigma&\approx7.594971610\end{align*}$$

To one decimal place, $\mu=76.1$ marks and $\sigma=7.6$ marks. Retain the unrounded values for subsequent calculations.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the z-score of the student who scored the highest on the test? Answer to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
The highest score is $88$. Using the unrounded statistics from part a:

$$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\\z&=\frac{88-76.0625}{\sqrt{93491/16-(1217/16)^2}}\\z&\approx1.571763611\\z&\approx1.6\quad\text{(1 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Mason was absent for this task, but his mark is usually 1.9 standard deviations below the mean. What mark should his teacher give him as an estimate? Answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
Below the mean gives $z=-1.9$. Using the unrounded statistics from part a:

$$\begin{align*}x&=\mu+z\sigma\\x&=76.0625-1.9\sqrt{93491/16-(1217/16)^2}\\x&\approx61.63205394\\x&\approx61.63\quad\text{(2 d.p.)}\end{align*}$$

The estimated mark is $61.63$ out of $100$.
